recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core follow-up is needed for FHIR-15698; future changes to the coverage-copay-type code definitions or displays should go through HL7 terminology governance rather than this core checkout.
issue_request: FHIR-15698 was Published and resolved Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It asked to add deductible and maximum annual out-of-pocket concepts, with the final resolution directing that deductible and maxannualoutofpocket be added to the Coverage.costToBeneficiary.type example code set.
initial_application: Git commit 7fbe7046270ff6857644a6af63207642576dc7ef, whose message included GF #15698, added deductible and maxoutofpocket concepts to source/coverage/codesystem-coverage-copay-type.xml. The current worker branch contains that historical application.
additional_context: Coverage is active in the current core build. The current Coverage StructureDefinition binds Coverage.costToBeneficiary.type to http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/coverage-copay-type, and the value set composes all codes from http://terminology.hl7.org/CodeSystem/coverage-copay-type. Commit 5c0494aacfd0b8bd52bc72c587aa89d0a64246f8 intentionally removed UTG/THO CodeSystem content from core, and the current THO CodeSystem version 1.0.1 still contains deductible and maxoutofpocket. FHIR-32966 later refined Coverage cost details with category, network, unit, and term elements, including annual maxoutofpocket examples.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current core source already points to the authoritative terminology source that contains the requested concepts, so editing core would be redundant and potentially in the wrong repository.

related_jiras.note: Later Coverage work added category, network, unit, and term to express details such as annual individual or family maximum out-of-pocket amounts while reusing type=maxoutofpocket.
The same historical GF commit family touched Coverage copay type terminology typo cleanup, but it is a separate editorial issue and was not decided here.
